sources.title: OpenVINO 2026 System Requirements
verified_facts: OpenVINO documents CPU, Intel GPU, and Intel NPU targets with device-specific operating-system and driver requirements.
GPU and NPU support may require drivers or operating-system changes outside the OpenVINO package.

sources.title: OpenVINO Automatic Device Selection
verified_facts: AUTO discovers compatible devices and chooses from a priority list.
The default performance hint is LATENCY; throughput hints require asynchronous inference to provide their intended benefit.

sources.title: OpenVINO Supported Devices
verified_facts: OpenVINO exposes CPU, GPU, and NPU devices plus AUTO, HETERO, and automatic batching modes.
Feature availability differs by device, so a generic OpenVINO result is not a device-specific compatibility result.

sources.title: ONNX Runtime OpenVINO Execution Provider
verified_facts: ONNX Runtime can register OpenVINO as an execution provider with explicit provider options.
Execution-provider configuration belongs in the benchmark manifest because provider behavior is not implied by the ONNX artifact alone.

sources.title: TensorRT Support Matrix
verified_facts: The current matrix exposes compatibility across TensorRT 10.x and 11.x releases and hardware precision capabilities.
Serialized engines are not generally portable across platforms and, without compatibility modes, are not portable across GPU architectures.

sources.title: TensorRT Precision Control
verified_facts: TensorRT 11 uses strongly typed networks.
Independent engine builds are not necessarily bit-identical because tactic timing and floating-point accumulation order can vary.

sources.title: DeepStream 9.0 Release Notes
verified_facts: DeepStream 9.0 has exact platform and accelerator support boundaries and documents known limitations.
Its Python bindings are deprecated in favor of pyservicemaker, which affects any future language and integration decision.

sources.title: DeepStream Gst-nvstreammux
verified_facts: nvstreammux batches frames across inputs and pushes a batch when full or when the configured timeout expires.
Batch size, timeout, scaling, source lifecycle, and source metadata are part of pipeline behavior and must be benchmarked together.

sources.title: Triton Inference Server 26.07 Release Notes
verified_facts: Triton ships as a versioned container with a coupled CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, and operating-system stack.
A Triton version therefore cannot be selected independently from driver, platform, backend, and container review.

sources.title: Triton Batchers
verified_facts: Dynamic batching is intended for stateless models and exposes queue delay, queue size, priority, timeout, and ordering controls.
Stateful sequences require sequence-aware scheduling; stream-local tracking cannot be treated as an ordinary stateless detector batch.

sources.title: Kubernetes Device Plugins
verified_facts: Vendor device plugins advertise integer extended resources such as GPUs.
Extended resources cannot be overcommitted and ordinary device resources cannot be shared between containers without a vendor-specific mechanism.

sources.title: GPU Operator With MIG
verified_facts: MIG exposes hardware-partitioned GPU instances on supported devices and requires an explicit cluster strategy and node configuration.
Changing MIG geometry disrupts GPU workloads and can require node reboot, so it is an operational change rather than a transparent scheduler choice.

sources.title: Time-Slicing GPUs In Kubernetes
verified_facts: Time slicing oversubscribes a GPU but does not provide MIG-style memory or fault isolation.
Shared GPU requests do not guarantee proportional compute, so time slicing cannot be assumed safe for hard latency or isolation requirements.

sources.title: MLPerf Inference Rules
verified_facts: Inference benchmarks bind the complete system under test, quality requirement, workload scenario, latency, throughput, and reproducibility rules.
Single-stream, multi-stream, server, and offline scenarios measure different properties and are not interchangeable.

sources.title: OCI Image Manifest Specification
verified_facts: OCI manifests bind image configuration and layers through content digests.
Deployment evidence should use immutable manifest digests rather than mutable tags.

sources.title: SLSA 1.2 Provenance
verified_facts: Provenance records where, when, and how an artifact was produced.
Compiled runtime artifacts and container images need verifiable source and build bindings in addition to a checksum.

sources.title: CycloneDX SBOM Lifecycle Guidance
verified_facts: CycloneDX 1.6 can describe software and machine-learning components and their provenance.
Runtime, model, driver-facing package, configuration, and container inventories should be reviewed as one deployment bill of materials.
